review_method: Independent original-map pixel inspection, complete source and baseline-rendered ring plots, registered outline and filled overlays, publication imprint and enlarged first-target southern-tip, second-target northeast and third-target southwest views. All 113 ordered positions across three single-ring Polygons were independently compared with the source, decoded geometries and summaries. The embedded GeoPDF affine was independently reopened and all registrations recomputed, including both rotation terms. The retained successful original acquisition receipt was verified against original bytes. Every selected position falls within an inspected original crop. Initial observations were recorded independently before comparison with separate research findings. Complete outlines, orientation, separate neighboring waters, mapped land, water-label typography and material omitted extensions were considered together; neither bounds nor label overlap alone established identity. The production decoder was not independently replayed by this reviewer.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory lake target IDs; repeated map labels do not increase the target count.

findings.follow_up_scope: Before assigning any whole-feature scalar name, resolve the High Hill and Silsby named-water partitions and southern-tip extent near Cuddle Lake against appropriately authorized detailed evidence. This is a name-scope hold, not an access failure.
findings.supported_name_scope: High Hill Lake and Silsby Lake are distinct associations within one selected ring, not aliases or a single whole-feature identity. The single selected ring combines High Hill Lake and Silsby Lake associations, which are non-exhaustive. Its southern tip crosses mapped land north of the separately labelled Cuddle Lake basin, and no exact named-water assignment is established for that tip. Detailed eastern continuations, shorelines, islands and narrow connections are generalized or omitted. Exact named-water partitions and complete detailed named-lake extents remain unverified. Exact extent and product-name application are not approved.
limits: The single selected ring combines High Hill Lake and Silsby Lake associations, which are non-exhaustive. Its southern tip crosses mapped land north of the separately labelled Cuddle Lake basin, and no exact named-water assignment is established for that tip. Detailed eastern continuations, shorelines, islands and narrow connections are generalized or omitted. Exact named-water partitions and complete detailed named-lake extents remain unverified.

Cuddle Lake is separately labelled along the narrow southern basin. Its label overlaps the selected southern-tip margin, but label overlap alone does not establish a third component association. Utik River is separately labelled east; Utik Lake and Bigstone Lake are separate southern neighboring waters.

One retained official Manitoba Geological Survey publication supports the associations. One provincial-government publisher group is represented; underlying hydrographic dataset independence and formal naming-registry authority are unverified.
No Korean form or additional whole-feature alias is certified; registered overlays do not establish surveyed shores or exact name partitions.
